Half-orcs don't do well, but you're playing an orc. I'm assuming from here: http://paizo.com/pathfinderRPG/prd/advancedRaceGuide/featuredRaces/orcs.html

That -2 intelligence hurts. Changing to a sorcerer is equally painful (-2 Cha). Your potentially low stats will give issues along the way, but the Eschew Materials feat is awesome at first level.

I'd stylize the orc as the not-so-macho orc who uses his magic to show other orcs how much of a real-orc he is.

Look for things to give you an advantage. If you can acquire orc henchmen to do your bidding, it might behoove you to take item creation feats to buff up your meat shields. I go with a bonded item over a familiar. Your +4 strength is going to let you lift a lot and do a lot of melee damage, so a bonded weapon (melee weapon) is ideal (forget the club or dagger and go with quarterstaff). True Strike (divination) would be a good personal orc spell, but Magic Weapon (transmutation) could help you or your grunts. Cause Fear (necromancy) would make just as much sense.

Work with your GM to get the orc racial spells (it'll make you stand out).

As for general wizard tips:

This discussion: http://paizo.com/threads/rzs2l8xh?Build-your-best-pathfinder-wizard-Level-120 is full of awesome ideas for builds.

This character sheet is mentioned in that thread and is a powerful 15th level character, you might peruse it for ideas on what to take when. http://www.mediafire.com/download/2yg0zonmq1c/Gilgeam+Grayhem+%2815th-level+human+mage+killer%29.pdf is of a human wizard who specializes in going first and ending a fight before it starts with his heightened flesh to stone spell. His DCs are hard to beat and he blows through SR nearly every time.
